items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: And good players, like Charlie Shavers and the guy that played with the, you know what I mean, what’s his name... Gleason. ... And he couldn’t get along with Benny Goodman. And Charlie Shavers couldn’t get along with him.

ctx.x: Tell us about playing with Benny Goodman.

Oh. I was with, I had a trio down on Broadway called Jack Silverman’s International, you never heard of it. He had great reviews, like he brought the reviews from Europe, those big casinos. Jack Silverman. He had, a lot of people don’t know about that. He had a place right down on Fifty-something street, right across from the old Palladium, right. He had one of the greatest nightclubs and he, I played down there with a big band and a show band they called it. And I played with the relief band — I only had…

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: I'd hear Charlie Shavers, I wanted to throw my horn away.

ctx.x: I wanted to play. I wanted to play, that was the only thing. And I was confused. Cause then I'd hear Charlie Shavers, I wanted to throw my horn away. I said

I'd hear what is this? Damn, Roy at the Three Deuces, what the hell is this, then I'd come and I'd hear Jabbo. I'd hear Cuban Cube, man, I didn't know what to do, I said, damn, that was my problem. I wanted to play. Money didn't mean anything to me. That's why I worked for Sam Wooding for $75.00 to Europe. I wasn't worried about money, because I was sitting beside Tommy Ladner, side-talking to Ladner.
